[Add to Google Preferred Sources](https://www.google.com/preferences/source?q=finance.biggo.com)

This week, the global memory chip industry entered a new wave of massive investment. Micron Technology announced plans to invest over $250 billion in the US by 2035, aiming to manufacture 40% of its DRAM output domestically — a significant increase from last year's plan. Benefiting from tight industry supply and explosive AI demand, Chinese companies posted stellar results: GigaDevice expects first-half net profit to surge roughly 11-fold, while Foxconn Industrial Internet projects net profit growth of 93% to 101%. SK Hynix's CEO went further, predicting that the memory chip supply shortage could persist beyond 2030. In the AI application layer, Apple suddenly sued OpenAI for systematically stealing trade secrets, casting a shadow over the latter's IPO process. Meanwhile, the model race between OpenAI and Anthropic is intensifying, while Elon Musk's SpaceXAI entered the market with a cost-efficiency strategy.
